title: If, Wish, Maybe
canDo: You can talk about what might happen, what didn't, and what should have

grammar.title: Real conditions
grammar.body: agar + past form, to + future: agar barish hui to hum nahin jayenge (if it rains, we won't go). The past form here means 'once that has happened'.

grammar.title: Unreal conditions and wishes
grammar.body: Both halves in the -ta form: agar main wahan hota to madad karta. kaash main wahan hota (I wish I were there). kaash aap ne bataya hota (I wish you had told me).

grammar.title: The subjunctive (short form)
grammar.body: Drop -ga/-gi/-ge from the future: aayega → aaye, aayenge → aayein. Used after shayad (maybe), zaroori hai ke (it's necessary that), chahta hoon ke (I want that), Allah kare (may God), jab tak … na (until).

grammar.title: Should have
grammar.body: mujhe aana chahiye tha (I should have come). The person takes ko/mujhe/tumhein; the verb stays in the -na form.

lessons.title: Agar… to…
lessons.blurb: If this, then that. The backbone of every plan and every threat.
lessons.canDo: You can say what will happen if something else does

teach.title: Real ifs
teach.info: agar (if) … to (then) …. For things that might really happen, Urdu often puts the 'if' half in the past form even though it means the future: agar barish hui (if it 'rained') to hum nahin jayenge.

teach.tip: The most common soft no in the language.
warna = otherwise. Every parent's favourite word.
jab tak … na = until. Note the 'na': literally 'as long as I don't say'.

lessons.title: Kaash
lessons.blurb: Wishes and what-ifs. The grammar of regret.
lessons.canDo: You can talk about things that didn't happen and wish they had

teach.title: Unreal ifs use hota
teach.info: For things that didn't happen, both halves take the -ta form: agar main wahan hota to madad karta (if I had been there, I would have helped). kaash + hota = I wish.

teach.tip: aap ki jagah = in your place. Advice, with deniability.

exercises.question: What happened?

options.feedback: mil jati = 'would have been caught'. It wasn't.
No. The flight left. Without them.

exercises.setup: Departures hall. Two suitcases, one argument.

exercises.prompt: Real plan or just a wish?
exercises.explain: hota / deta / bataya hota: it didn't happen.
A wish about something unreal: hota.
You aren't in their place, so it's hota (were), not hoon (am).

lessons.title: Shayad
lessons.blurb: Maybe, possibly, who knows. How to commit to nothing.
lessons.canDo: You can say how likely something is

teach.title: Maybe takes the short form
teach.info: After shayad, the verb drops its ending: woh aayega (he will come) → shayad woh aaye (maybe he'll come). This short form is the subjunctive: for things that are possible, wanted or needed, not certain.

teach.tip: lagta hai = it seems. Add it to any sentence to make it an opinion.

exercises.explain: After shayad the verb is the short form: aaye.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks when the electricity will come back.

lessons.title: Should have
lessons.canDo: You can say what should have happened and what you want for someone

teach.tip: chahiye = should. chahiye tha = should have.
zaroori hai ke + short form. Same subjunctive as after shayad.
'I want that you stay happy.' Urdu needs the 'ke'.

exercises.explain: chahiye takes mujhe, even in the past.
After zaroori hai ke: the short form, aayein.

exercises.prompt: Your cousin has an exam tomorrow.

boss.title: The Surprise Visit
boss.blurb: You turned up at Khala's unannounced. Every sentence she says starts with 'if'.
boss.scene: You were in the neighbourhood, so you rang Khala's bell. She is delighted and also slightly offended: she had no time to cook.
boss.canDo: You can handle ifs, wishes and should-haves in a real conversation

options.reaction: A wish in the past. She's impressed despite herself.
She knows what 'agar waqt mila' means. She has used it herself.

end.title: Hypothetically fluent
end.text: Ifs, wishes, maybes and should-haves, all with the right verb forms. There was no biryani today. There will be a great deal tomorrow.
